dmitri: FYI onboarding Artemis-9B (orig: mistral-style freqs, tokenizer: merged-bpe-spm-union) -> int3/int4 builds. Saw a weird 'token-stick' degenerate behavior on booklong at ~2800 tokens. Loop size varies 2-6 tokens.

wei: can you paste repro? model file, tokenizer, seq len, sampling?

dmitri: Artemis9B_bf16 -> Artemis9B_int3 and int4. Tokenizer: vocab-union-v1 (we unioned original spm vocab with a bpe fallback to make cross-model intake easy). Seq=4096, temp=0.0 greedy. Batch=1.

clare: union vocabs are risky if we remap ids naively. We had one case where two different byte sequences collapsed into a single id after packer dedupe.

dmitri: token ids at collapse (snippet):
```
[4021, 999, 4021, 999, 4021, 999, 156, 202]
```
Looks like a two-id motif repeats then drifts.

ci-bot: quick-eval queued: run_eval --model Artemis9B_int4 --task booklong --seq 4096 --runs 6

ci-bot: quick-eval result: 5/6 runs show degeneracy onset 2720-2890. Top-1 tokens dominate distribution; perplexity spike logged.

olivia: any rotary table diffs in conversion path? we convert mistral-style per-head freqs -> standard rotary table with headwise scaling. Small rounding errors could push angles across the wrap boundary.

dmitri: compared pre/post conversion L-inf on cos/sin tables for layer 8 head 2 first 32 dims: max diff ~0.008 for int4 packer. That's larger than expected.

mike: int3 packer is even more aggressive. Did you try keeping rotary tables at higher precision only?

dmitri: yes: A) int4 with rotary stored as bf16 (other weights int4), B) int3 with rotary bf16. Commands:
```
# A
python infra/run_infer.py --model Artemis9B_int4 --rotary-precision bf16 --seq 4096
# B
python infra/run_infer.py --model Artemis9B_int3 --rotary-precision bf16 --seq 4096
```

ci-bot: Run A finished: degeneracy eliminated in 6/6 quick runs. Latency +5.3% compared to int4 baseline.

ci-bot: Run B finished: partial improvement; runs show onset pushed to ~3600 but 2/6 still collapse.

wei: that pattern implies numeric error in rotary accumulation is dominant; int3 is borderline even if rotary uses bf16. Also tokenizer union aliasing amplifies the local attractor.

clare: can you dump token union mapping for the repeated ids? maybe two distinct sequences were assigned same id after union-sufix normalization.

dmitri: mapping snippet: id 4021 -> [b"e\xCC\x81" (e + combining acute), b"\xE9" (precomposed é)] We normalized NFKC before union, but packer then deduped similar byte sequences incorrectly.

olivia: wow, that's a normalization+dedupe bug. Two different unicode normalization forms ended up mapped to same byte key in the packer map. That can create aliasing for accented characters.

mike: mitigation path: 1) fix packer to canonicalize to NFD before byte-keying and keep mapping stable, 2) add converter check that reports any id collision where original codepoints differed, 3) for immediate fix keep rotary tables at bf16 and kv accumulation as fp32 for Artemis-int4/int3.

ci-bot: test: run with kv accumulation fp32 plus rotary bf16.

ci-bot: patched run: Artemis9B_int4 --rotary-precision bf16 --kv-accumulation fp32 -> result: degeneracy gone in 6/6. Perf +6.0%.

wei: good. for int3 we'll probably need a targeted exception: keep rotary and kv in higher precision or avoid int3 until packer changes land.

clare: opened issue #3220 in convertor: vocab-union dedupe on normalized bytes produced collisions. Draft PR to NFD-canonicalize before keying: https://github.com/redwood-inference/convertor/pull/3221

dmitri: opened internal PR #569 to store per-head rotary multipliers as bf16 and to add a longseq regression test (booklong seq=4096 greedy) that fails if repeating-id motif detected.

mike: add a nightly job for unioned-tokenizer models that runs longseq degens. Also add an onboarding checklist item: "validate rotary L-inf diff < 1e-4 after conversion".

olivia: release note draft: Artemis-9B int4/int3 advisory: to avoid rare long-context repetition when using unioned tokenizers, rotational constants and kv accumulation retained higher precision; we are fixing packer dedupe to preserve normalization uniqueness.

dmitri: assigning follow-ups: clare -> packer PR; wei -> perf analysis for bf16-rotary; mike -> nightly CI job; olivia -> release note.

mike: tagging infra and bench. cc @product for messaging. :white_check_mark:
